references.text: Here the grain offering (mincha) that the priests were to handle is described, and how a part of it belonged to Aaron and his sons.
The rest of the grain offering belonged to Aaron and his sons as a most holy portion of the Lord's fire offering.
The context for the grain offering that the priests were to eat, in contrast to the priest's own grain offering which had to be burned completely.
Further regulations concerning the grain offering and who among the priests it belonged to.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple confirms that the grain offering, sin offering, and guilt offering belong to the priests.
The term 'kalil' (wholly burnt) is also used for the burnt offering which was to be burned completely on the altar.
The preceding verse describing how the grain offering was to be offered as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
